answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-backed identity with slashing: every agent must lock a bond before its vote counts, so influence is bought with capital, not names. The bond works like a velvet rope, easy to approach yet expensive to pass, and it builds a bridge from a cheap pseudonym to real economic value. An attacker minting N fake identities must post N separate bonds, so the cost grows linearly with each Sybil while each fake vote keeps the same weight; worse, a detected double-vote slashes the whole bond, leaving the cheater on a narrow ledge where one mistake forfeits everything.
